question_en: An analyst has compiled the following data on a corporate bond: The price impact from an instantaneous 80 basis points of spread narrowing is closest to (%):
explanation_en: The price change of a bond is a function of its modified duration, its convexity, and a change in its yield. The yield of a corporate bond is a function of interest rates and the bond's yield spread. The yield spread is the difference in yields between the corporate bond and a government issue of the same maturity, reflecting the greater credit and liquidity risks (ie, spread risk) of the corporate bond. A change in spread can significantly impact the price of a bond. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions. Therefore, narrowing spreads (ie, smaller spreads) positively impact prices and widening spreads (ie, larger spreads) have a negative impact. Note that the negative sign in the price impact equation accounts for this inverse relationship. Price impact can be determined by entering the values into the formula: (Choice A) 6.86% is the estimated price decline if the spread widens by 80 basis points. (Choice B) 7.15% results from approximating price impact (L54761) using only modified duration, which is appropriate for only small changes in spreads.

question_en: The kinked demand curve oligopoly model is based on a belief that:
option_a: competing rms that collude to restrict output each have an incentive to cheat. a rm’s competitors will follow a price decrease but will not follow a price
option_b: increase. a rm can increase prots by charging dierent prices to distinct groups of
explanation_en: In the kinked demand curve oligopoly model, the demand curve facing each firm is more elastic above the current price and less elastic below the current price, because the other firms in the industry will likely match a price decrease by one firm but will not match a price increase. The incentive to cheat on price collusion agreements is illustrated by game theory. Price discrimination is the method by which a price seeking firm can increase profits by charging different prices to consumers in distinct groups with differing price elasticity of demand.

question_en: Investing cash flows most likely reflect changes in which of the firm's balance sheet items?
explanation_en: Investing cash flows are most closely linked to a firm's noncurrent assets. Operating cash flows are most closely linked to a firm's current assets and current liabilities. Financing cash flows are most closely linked to a firm's noncurrent liabilities and equity.

question_en: Which form of the efficient markets hypothesis (EMH) implies that an investor can achieve positive abnormal returns on average by using technical analysis?
explanation_en: An investor cannot achieve positive abnormal returns on average by using technical analysis if prices fully reflect all available security market (price and volume) information. The weak form of the EMH assumes prices reflect this information, and the semistrong and strong forms assume prices reflect additional (non-market) information as well.

question_en: Which of the following hedge fund mechanisms is most likely used to impose a temporary restriction on redemptions if needed?
explanation_en:
A gate is a mechanism that a hedge fund manager can invoke on an as-needed basis to temporarily limit or restrict investor redemptions, typically during periods of high redemption requests or illiquid market conditions — it is the tool used to impose a restriction only when needed.

(Choice B) A notice period requires investors to give advance notice before redeeming, but does not itself restrict redemptions.
(Choice C) A lockup period is a fixed, predetermined period (agreed at the time of investment) during which no redemptions are permitted at all — it is not an as-needed, temporary restriction.

question_en: Snow Blower Industries operates in an increasing price environment and uses the FIFO method for inventory reporting. Compared to the weighted average cost method, Snow Blower's use of the FIFO method will most likely decrease:
explanation_en: Under FIFO, Snow Blower will report lower cost of goods sold because the first items bought are assumed to be the units sold, and these have the lowest cost in a rising price environment. Net income is higher under FIFO in an increasing price environment because lower cost of goods sold results in higher income. Ending inventory is higher under FIFO in an increasing price environment.

subtopic: 7.07 Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Fixed-Rate Bonds
question_en: A three-year, zero-coupon bond is priced at 80 per 100 of par value. The annual yield-to-maturity (YTM), stated with a periodicity of 6, is closest to:
explanation_en:
HP 12c TI BA II Plus
The annual YTM is a standardized measure that allows investors to compare bonds with maturities greater than one year. The annual YTM of a
bond depends on the rate per compounding period (periodic rate) and the number of compounding periods per year (periodicity).
Compounding periods per year is typically the number of coupon payments per year. For example, for a fixed-income bond with semiannual
coupons, the periodicity is 2.
Periodicity for a zero-coupon bond is arbitrary since the bond does not pay coupons. In this question, the periodicity is given as 6 (ie, there are six
compounding periods per year). The annual YTM is derived from the bond price formula shown above and calculated using a financial calculator:
(Choice A) 3.74% results from annualizing the rate by the years to maturity (3), not the periodicity (6).
(Choice C) 7.72% results from using 3 (the years to maturity) for (n × m).

question_en: Investor overreaction that has been documented in securities markets is most likely attributable to investors exhibiting:
explanation_en: Loss aversion refers to the tendency for investors to dislike downside risks more than upside risks creating asymmetrical risk preferences. This dislike of losses may be a cause of investor overreaction. The standard economic notion of risk aversion assumes symmetric risk preferences. Conservatism is the behavioral bias whereby investors react slowly to new information and is unlikely to cause overreaction.

question_en: A company has 10 million shares of common stock outstanding and has not issued or repurchased common stock this year. It issued 300,000 employee stock options several years ago, which are presently exercisable at $40 per share. The average market price per share for the company's stock this year is $30. It also paid dividends of $1 million on its nonconvertible preferred stock. If the company has a net income of $11 million this year, the company's reported EPS will be closest to:
explanation_en:
Employee stock options, if exercised, will increase the number of shares outstanding. This causes earnings per share (EPS) to decrease since
net income is divided by a larger number of shares. Employee stock options are dilutive securities. The general rule is that all dilutive securities
are converted to common stock or, in the case of options, exercised at the beginning of the period.
For employee stock options, this presumption of exercise is valid only if the stock's average market price exceeds the option's exercise price.
Exercising an option must make economic sense, which is not the case by paying $40 for a share worth $30. The options will not be exercised in
this case, so the weighted average number of shares will not change. Basic EPS is calculated as follows:
(Choice B) Under these assumptions, the options would not be exercised since it would be economically unsound to do so. If they were, the
treasury stock method would result in the company having 100,000 fewer shares outstanding, or 9.9 million weighted average number of shares
for the period. Dividing $10 million ($11 million net income − $1 million preferred dividend) by 9.9 million shares results in an EPS of $1.01.
(Choice C) Preferred dividends are paid from net income, so they are not available to the common shareholders. The EPS of $1.10 results from
neglecting to first subtract the preferred dividends from net income before dividing by the weighted average number of common shares.

question_en: Which of the following best describes loss severity for a debt instrument?
explanation_en:
Credit risk refers to the expected financial loss that occurs if a bond issuer defaults in paying interest and/or principal. Expected loss comprises
two components, the probability that a default occurs and the severity of the loss. Loss severity, also known as loss given default, is the
portion of a bond's value, including unpaid interest, that a bond investor loses when an issuer defaults:
Loss severity = (1 − recovery rate)
The recovery rate is the principal amount recovered in a default, expressed as a percentage of par. When defaults do occur, the severity of the
loss can range from a total loss to a complete recovery of principal and interest.
(Choice B) Loss severity is expressed as (1 − recovery rate), not (1 − default rate).
(Choice C) Loss severity is expressed as (1 − recovery rate), not (par value × default probability).

question_en: A client instructs a broker to submit a limit order to buy 10,000 shares of a stock at £15 a share. This is best described as a(n):
explanation_en:
Traders send various order instructions to intermediaries (eg, brokers, dealers, exchanges) to place trades. Execution instructions define how
an order is filled, commonly in the form of a market or limit order. A market order prioritizes the speed of execution, whereas a limit order
prioritizes the price. Here, the client instructs the broker to execute the buy limit order only if the price is £15 or below.
(Choice A) Validity instructions specify when an order is filled.
(Choice B) Clearing instructions state how a trade is settled.

question_en: A trader buys shares of a stock on margin: Based on this information, the margin call price is closest to:
explanation_en:
Investors often borrow money from brokerages to finance portions of a stock purchase (ie, buying on margin). As time passes, the trader's equity
amounts to the value of the stock position net of the margin loan. Downward stock price movements decrease the trader's equity percentage
(equity / value of total stock position), which increases risk to the lender for recovering principal.
Brokerage lenders protect their loaned money by imposing a maintenance margin requirement, which specifies the trader's minimum equity
percentage (40%). If the equity percentage drops below 40% (from stock price declines), then the investor must contribute additional equity.
Otherwise, the brokerage will sell the entire stock position and recoup the loan. The margin call price (233.33) is the stock price that triggers a
margin call .
To conceptually grasp the calculation, understand that the investor initially contributed €560 (denoted E) per share in equity (80% of purchase
i
price × €700 a share). If the stock price drops to €233.33, the trader's equity per share amounts to €93.33, or [560 + (233.33 − 700)]. This results
in an equity percentage of 40% (or 93.33 / 233.33), which equals the maintenance margin. Effectively, if the stock price falls below 233.33, the
investor will receive a margin call since the remaining equity percentage will be below the 40% maintenance margin.
(Choice B) €350.00 results from incorrectly setting 60% (or 1 − 0.4) as the maintenance margin.
(Choice C) €420.00 results from reducing the initial stock price of €700 by 40%.

subtopic: 7.06 Fixed-Income Bond Valuation Prices and Yields
question_en: On August 8, 20X0, an investor buys a 6.4%, semiannual-paying bond with a YTM of 5.2%. The bond matures on December 15, 20X2 and pays coupon interest each June 15 and December 15. The bond trades on a 30/360 basis. If the dealer quotes a price of 102.62 per 100 of par value, the bond's flat price on August 8, 20X0 is closest to:
explanation_en: A bond's flat price is the difference between its full price and any interest that accrued since it last paid coupon interest. When selling a bond, dealers usually quote a bond's flat price as the market price. The accrued interest is added to the flat price, and the buyer pays the total amount. It should be noted that the flat price is also known as the "clean price" and that the full price is also known as the "dirty price." The exam may use any of these terms in questions related to this topic. (Choice A) 101.68 results from incorrectly assuming 102.62 is the bond's full price. Fifty-three days of interest accrued between June 15 and August 8, 20X0. The total accrued interest is (53 ÷ 180) × 3.2, or approximately 0.94 per 100 par value. Subtracting that amount from 102.62 equals 101.68. Note: The calculator keystrokes that are included with this question refer to this calculation. (Choice C) 103.56 is the bond's full price on August 8, 20X0.

question_en: A low inventory turnover ratio in a period of declining revenue growth is most likely an indication that a firm may have:
explanation_en: Low inventory turnover and declining revenue growth may be signs that a firm has obsolete or slow-moving inventory. High turnover and low revenue growth may indicate too little inventory, while high turnover and high revenue growth may indicate efficient inventory management.

question_en: Which provision of an alternative investment partnership's incentive fees is designed to prevent investors from paying multiple incentive fees for the same performance?
explanation_en: If a partnership has a high water mark, incentive fees are based on increases in investors' accounts above their highest previous values. As a result, managers do not receive incentive fees on returns that reverse previous losses. A hurdle rate is a minimum return a manager must achieve in a given period to become eligible to receive incentive fees. A clawback provision enables the limited partners to recover incentive fees paid to the manager in earlier periods if subsequent losses negate some of the gains on which those incentive fees were based.

question_en: Which of the following is least likely a unique risk of property development?
explanation_en: When a development uses leverage, default risk increases because the investment is riskier. However, default risk applies to investments that use leverage; this is not unique to real estate development. Regulatory issues, including environmental regulations and zoning permits, can prevent a real estate development project from moving forward. Construction delays can change the economics of the investment due to changing market conditions and the impact of the time value of money on the IRR.

question_en: A portfolio manager creates an index for internal benchmarking, consisting of 1,000 shares of 20 different securities. This index is best characterized as a(n):
explanation_en: By allocating equal numbers of shares to each constituent, the manager has created a price-weighted index. An equal-weighted index would allocate an equal money amount to each share. A market-capitalization-weighted index would include shares according to their market value, which assumes neither equal number nor equal money value of shares.

subtopic: 7.12 Yield-Based Bond Convexity and Portfolio Properties
question_en: A noncallable bond has an annual modified duration of 9.12. If the bond's yield decreases by 0.18% and its convexity adjustment is 0.21%, then the bond's percentage change in price is closest to:
explanation_en:
When a noncallable bond's yield changes, one way to estimate its price change is to add together the price change due to duration and the price
change due to convexity. The price change due to duration is a linear approximation. The convexity adjustment, which is always positive for
noncallable bonds, is added to the percentage price change due to duration to obtain an estimate of the bond's percentage price change.
This scenario gives the bond's annual modified duration, yield change, and convexity adjustment. To calculate the percentage price change of the
bond, substitute the data as follows:
%∆PVFull = (−9.12 × −0.0018) + 0.0021
= 0.016416 + 0.0021
= 0.018516
≈ 1.85%
The sum is only an estimate. The actual new price of the bond will be the present value of its promised future cash flows based on the new YTM.
(Choice A) −1.43% results from mistakenly assuming that the change in yield is positive.
(Choice C) 3.74% results from substituting 0.021 for the convexity adjustment instead of 0.0021.

question_en: Which of the following is most likely a disclosure for PPE that is required under IFRS but not under US GAAP?
option_c: Estimated depreciation over the next five years
explanation_en:
Required disclosures of property, plant, and equipment (PPE) vary between IFRS and US GAAP. Under US GAAP, required disclosures are
much less detailed as compared to IFRS. PPE includes tangible assets with useful lives of greater than one year. The costs (ie, measurement
base) to obtain them are capitalized. Each year, part of the PPE cost is expensed as depreciation. Disclosures help analysts identify how different
companies determine original costs and calculate depreciation expenses.
The disclosure of assets' useful lives is required exclusively under IFRS. Useful life is an estimate of the time remaining in which an asset
continues to provide economic benefit (eg, generate revenue).
(Choice B) Both IFRS and US GAAP require the disclosure of the gross carrying amount. The gross carrying amount is the value of an asset
prior to accounting for deprecation.
(Choice C) The disclosure of estimated depreciation over the next five years is required under US GAAP, not IFRS.

question_en: A mutual fund contains 250 constituent companies. ● 12% of the companies are categorized as healthcare stocks. ● 16% of the companies are categorized as small-cap stocks. ● 4% of the companies are categorized as both healthcare and small-cap stocks. If the categories are not mutually exclusive, then the probability that any constituent company is a healthcare or small-cap stock is closest to:
explanation_en:
For events that are not mutually exclusive, the probability that at least one event will occur equals the sum of the individual events'
probabilities minus their joint probability (ie, P(A and B)). The joint probability that the stock is both a healthcare stock and a small-cap stock is
captured in the overlapping area in the diagram below. Since this overlapping area shares outcomes with Event A and Event B, P(A and B)
should be subtracted from the sum of their individual probabilities to avoid double counting.
(Choice B) 26.1% results from subtracting the product of P(A) and P(B) from the sum of P(A) and P(B). The joint probability of two events P(A
and B) cannot be calculated from multiplying the probabilities of two events in a non–mutually exclusive scenario.
(Choice C) 28.0% results from failing to subtract P(A and B) from the sum of P(A) and P(B).

question_en: Which archetype of globalization and cooperation provides the greatest contrast to multilateralism?
explanation_en: Globalization describes how companies, governments, and people transact across the world. Globalization involves some level of cooperation across countries to promote the exchange of information, goods and services, technology, and jobs. In modern times, both state and non-state actors (eg, companies) are the drivers behind globalization to access resources, markets, and profits across borders. In contrast, anti-globalization or nationalism is characterized by limited cooperation with other countries to promote a country's own self-interest. Historically, nationalistic governments have practiced policies that at times negatively impacted other countries. Most countries can be labeled as an archetype that falls on the spectrum of globalization and cooperation. A country that practices multilateralism (eg, Singapore) is very cooperative and open to globalization. Multilaterally oriented countries typically adopt beneficial trade terms to facilitate international business. In contrast, autarky describes a country that adopts nationalistic policies and seeks self-sufficiency through limited trade and little cooperation. (Choice B) Hegemony describes countries that are open to globalization but less cooperative (eg, United States, Russia, China). Hegemonic countries are often powerful global leaders who exert significant economic and political influence worldwide. (Choice C) Bilateralism is characterized by regionalism, where two countries cooperate with each other. Countries that practice bilateralism typically have customized relationships with each partner.

question_en: A corporation is evaluating two projects with the following cash flows (INR million): Project 1 has a required rate of return of 3% and an internal rate of return (IRR) of 26.9%, while Project 2 has a required rate of return of 8% and an IRR of 38.8%. If the projects are mutually exclusive, the most appropriate investment decision is to invest in:
explanation_en:
HP 12c TI BA II Plus
Net present value (NPV) analysis evaluates investments based on the present value of a project's cash flows. NPV is the difference between
the present values of the project's cash outflows and inflows. The projected cash flows are discounted to the present using the required rate
of return (r) as the discount rate. As a result, projects with a positive NPV add to company value.
Project 1 is the most appropriate investment choice in this scenario since it has a higher NPV than Project 2 and will therefore add more
shareholder value to the corporation.
(Choice B) Project 2 seems to be the better choice based on its higher internal rate of return (IRR); however, the NPV is a superior decision
criterion since NPV measures the actual value added to the company, whereas IRR measures a percentage return. A project can have a higher
percentage return but a smaller NPV, based on the timing of the cash flows and their discount rate, resulting in less value added to the
corporation.
(Choice C) Since the projects are mutually exclusive, the corporation cannot invest in both projects, although each has a positive NPV and would
add value.

question_en: Candram Truzz, CFA, is a financial advisor who practices in multiple jurisdictions. In his resident country, Country A, he is not required by law to hold a financial advisor’s license but he is required to uphold a fiduciary duty to his clients. In Country B, authorities require him to hold a financial advisor’s license, but he is not expected to uphold a fiduciary duty to his clients. In Country C, authorities require both a financial advisor’s license and an asset management license in addition to upholding a fiduciary responsibility toward clients. In which of the three countries does Truzz have the duty to adhere to the CFA Code and Standards over local laws?
explanation_en: Standard I–Professionalism requires members and candidates to comply with the more strict law, rule, or regulation in the event of conflicts of any applicable laws, rules, and regulations (including the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct). Country B does not require a financial advisor to uphold a fiduciary duty (as is required by Country A and C), i.e., put the client’s interest before their own, therefore the CFA Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct (Duty to Clients) would be applicable as it is the stricter of the two. A is incorrect because Country A requires the upholding of fiduciary duties that creates a higher standard than that of the Code and Standards. C is incorrect because Country C requires two licenses and the upholding of fiduciary duties that creates a higher standard than that of the Code and Standards. Thus Country C’s laws are the governing law.

subtopic: Reading 18 Capital Flows and the FX Market
question_en: Participants in foreign exchange markets that can be characterized as "real money accounts" most likely include:
explanation_en: Real money accounts are foreign exchange buy-side investors that do not use derivatives. Many mutual funds, pension funds, and insurance companies can be classified as real money accounts. Hedge funds typically use derivatives. Central banks usually do not act as investors in foreign exchange markets but may intervene in foreign exchange markets to achieve monetary policy objectives.

question_en: Which of the following is most likely a trade agreement in which barriers on the movement of labor and capital goods among members are removed, but members do not adopt common economic policies?
option_c: Common markets. 10 | P age CFA WITH KEVIN SIR - CFA LEVEL 1 - 2024 MOCK EXAM
explanation_en: In common markets, member countries remove all the restrictions regarding import-export goods and services, adopt a standard set of trade restrictions on non-members, and remove barriers to labor and capital goods movement among members. However, members do not adopt common economic policies. A is incorrect. A monetary union is basically two or more governments coming together and agreeing to share a common currency. B is incorrect. In an economic union, members adopt common economic policies on regulating products, capital and labor, and freedom of movement of goods and services.
